<STRUCT_0001>
It often happens one can prove the members of a covering of a scheme
have a certain property. In many cases this implies the scheme has the
property too. For example, if <MATH_0001> is a scheme, and <MATH_0002>
is a surjective flat morphism such that <MATH_0003> is a reduced scheme, then <MATH_0004> is
reduced. You can prove this by looking at local rings and using
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0001>.
We say that the property of being reduced
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>descends through flat surjective morphisms<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>.
Some results of this type are collected in
Algebra, Section <REF_0002> and
for schemes in Section <REF_0003>.
Some analogous results on descending properties
of morphisms are in Section <REF_0004>.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
On the other hand, there are examples of surjective flat morphisms
<MATH_0005> with <MATH_0006> reduced and <MATH_0007> not, for example the morphism
<MATH_0008>. Hence the property of
being reduced does not <TEXTITOPEN_0002>ascend along flat morphisms<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>. Having infinite
residue fields is a property which does ascend along flat morphisms (but
does not descend along surjective flat morphisms of course). Some results
of this type are collected in
Algebra, Section <REF_0005>.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
